verdict.rationale: ReelMimic builds a shared plan of storyboard, characters, assets and style frames that is approved before up to 6 agents build different shots. Its Production line tab tracks each character across the video, which points to shared character definitions spanning shots. However, nothing states or demonstrates that characters or scenes stay visually consistent from shot to shot, and following a user's own designs (docs-11) is a reference input, not proof of cross-shot consistency. missing for 10: explicit cross-shot character/scene consistency claim, a mechanism showing shared assets are enforced across shots, review checks for consistency, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a creator, a character or scene stays consistent across multiple generated shots, not just within one clip

citations.quote: Storyboard, characters, assets and a few style frames. Chat about it until you like it, then approve.
The Production line tab shows where each character and each part of the video is, with the review screenshots.
Up to 6 work on different parts of the video. Each finished shot goes to a new agent for review
